title: Fifths by estimate and adjust
li: We are learning to make fifths of a length and to show them on a number line.
sc: I can make 5 equal parts of a length by estimating and adjusting
I can name and write fifths, like 2/5 and 4/5
I can mark fifths on a number line

slides.title: Warm-up: Thirds and counting
items: How many thirds make one whole?
Which is longer: 1/3 or 1/8 of the same strip?

slides.means: One of 5 equal parts of a whole. 5 fifths make one whole.
slides.example: A 50 cm stick cut into fifths has 5 parts of 10 cm.

slides.title: I do: Make fifths
slides.problem: Make fifths of a paper strip without a ruler.

steps.label: Estimate
steps.text: 5 parts is more than 4, so 1/5 is a bit shorter than 1/4. Mark your guess lightly.

steps.label: Check
steps.text: Step that length along the strip 5 times.

steps.label: Adjust
steps.text: Bit left over? Make the part longer. Ran out? Make it shorter.

steps.label: Done
steps.text: When 5 parts fit exactly, label them 1/5, 2/5, 3/5, 4/5, 5/5.

slides.notes: Show the estimate going too long this time, so students see the other kind of adjustment. Link back to thirds: same method, different number of parts.

slides.title: Fifths on a number line

rows.label: Tenths
rows.text: Halve each fifth and you get 10 parts: tenths.

slides.notes: Ask: is there a mark for 1/2 on this line? Let students find that 1/2 sits between 2/5 and 3/5.

slides.title: Turn and talk
slides.prompt: Why is it harder to make fifths than quarters? What helps you get a good first estimate?
slides.notes: Quarters can be folded by halving. Fifths cannot. A good estimate: a bit shorter than a quarter, or about 2 fingers on a 15 cm strip.

slides.title: Which one?
slides.question: Which is longer: 1/5 or 1/3 of the same ribbon?
why: Wrong: this child thinks a bigger denominator means a bigger part. 5 parts means shorter parts.
Right: the ribbon is cut into fewer parts, so each third is longer than each fifth.
Wrong: both are 1 part, but the parts are different sizes.
Wrong: we can reason without measuring, because it is the same ribbon.

slides.title: Show me: fifths
questions: How many fifths make one whole?
A 20 cm strip is cut into fifths. How long is each part?
Write the fraction for 4 of 5 equal parts.

slides.title: Activity: Five of a kind
steps: Estimate 1/5 of your strip and mark it lightly.
Step it out 5 times and adjust until it fits.
Label 1/5 to 5/5. Glue it above a number line.
Do your level on the Fifths of a length sheet.
slides.notes: Strips of 20, 25 or 35 cm give whole centimetre fifths for checking.

slides.support: Use a strip 10 squares long. Mark every 2 squares to make fifths, then check by measuring.
slides.core: Make fifths of 2 strips. Mark fifths on number lines and find fifths of lengths in cm.
slides.extend: Halve fifths to make tenths. Which tenths land on a fifth? Where does 1/2 go on a fifths line?

questions: How is making fifths like making thirds?
Where does 1/2 sit on a fifths number line? Is it on a mark?
slides.connect: We made fifths by estimating and adjusting and placed them on a number line. Show a partner which success criteria you met.
slides.notes: Finish the Thirds and fifths panel of the flip book.

teach.text: Fifths are 5 equal parts. Each part is 1/5. Five fifths make one whole.

items.q: How many fifths make one whole?
A 10 cm strip is cut into fifths. How long is each part?

teach.text: Count the spaces from 0. Each space is 1/5. 5/5 lands on 1.

items.q: What fraction is marked with the dot?
How long is 3/5 of a 50 cm strip?
Ana's first try at 1/5 was 6 cm. Stepped out 5 times, 5 cm was left over. Should her part be longer or shorter? How long is the strip?
items.answer: Longer. The strip is 30 + 5 = 35 cm, so 1/5 should be 7 cm.

items.q: Order from shortest to longest (same strip): 1/3, 1/5, 1/2

teach.text: Halve each fifth to make tenths. 1/5 lines up with 2/10.

items.q: How long is 7/10 of a 50 cm strip?
Where does 1/2 go on this fifths line? Explain.
items.answer: Halfway between 2/5 and 3/5. It is not on a mark. It is the same as 5/10.

items.q: Ana's first try at 1/5 was 9 cm. Stepped out 5 times, it went 5 cm past the end. How long is the strip? What should 1/5 be?
items.answer: The strip is 45 - 5 = 40 cm, so 1/5 is 8 cm.

teacherNotes: Fifths are harder to estimate than thirds, so expect two or three adjustments. Encourage students to say whether each estimate was too long or too short before they move the mark. The hinge question tests the 'bigger denominator, bigger fraction' idea; answer it with two strips the same length. Tenths are only in the Spicy task; they are a related fraction formed by halving, named in the outcome.

exitTicket.q: Mark and label 3/5 on the number line.
Which is longer, 1/5 or 1/4 of the same strip? Why?
exitTicket.answer: 1/4. The strip is cut into fewer parts, so each part is longer.
